answer: Each new agent must post a slashable bond tied to a unique hardware enclave key, and its voting weight accrues only as independent peers attest its completed work in small increments. Padding with thousands of identities fails because every bond is at risk: if a cluster of clones vouches for itself, a random audit slashes all of them, so faking one honest opal of reputation costs real capital. At each dawn, the ledger recomputes weight from attested output alone, ensuring a dense island of fresh wallets earns nothing while its locked stake bleeds away.
